title: evict_if_needed could infinite loop if peers.remove fails to reduce len
description:
**File:** rust/lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs
**Lines:** 358-371 (ReplayProtector), 526-542 (LinkLayer)

**Issue:** The while loop 'while self.peers.len() > self.max_peers' relies on peers.remove() successfully reducing the map size. If remove() ever returns None (e.g., due to a bug where oldest_iid is stale), the loop would spin forever.

The current code does break on 'if let Some(iid) = oldest_iid ... else { break; }' which protects against empty maps, but the inner remove could theoretically fail if the HashMap is modified between finding oldest and removing.

**Trigger:** Theoretical only - requires concurrent modification or HashMap implementation bug.

**Bad behavior:** CPU spin in infinite loop.

**Suggested fix:** Use 'while let Some(oldest) = self.peers.iter().min_by_key(...).map(|(k,_)| *k) && self.peers.len() > self.max_peers { self.peers.remove(&oldest); ... }' pattern, or add iteration bound.
